title: Ulysses
author: James Joyce
description: One day, 16 June 1904, mapped street by street. Joyce said he wanted Dublin so exactly rendered it could be rebuilt from the book, and people have been walking it every Bloomsday since. From the Martello tower at Sandycove in the south to the graves at Glasnevin in the north, every place here is real and still findable.

route.summary: The book opens on the gunrest atop this squat granite tower at Sandycove, where Stephen Dedalus is lodging with Buck Mulligan and the Englishman Haines. By breakfast Stephen has resolved not to return, and hands over the key. It is a real Martello tower, one of a chain built against a French invasion; Joyce himself stayed here in 1904, and it is now the James Joyce Tower and Museum.

Alone on the ebb-tide sands, Stephen thinks his way through the whole visible and invisible world, the episode Joyce built as a single unbroken interior monologue. The same flat strand returns in the evening for Gerty MacDowell's chapter. It is a real beach on Dublin Bay, still walked at low water below the Sandymount seafront.
route.note: The episode names Sandymount strand explicitly. The pin marks a representative point on the open sands below Leahy's Terrace, where Stephen walks; the strand itself runs for more than a kilometre.

route.summary: We meet Leopold Bloom in his own kitchen, frying a kidney and carrying up his wife Molly's breakfast, before he steps out into the morning. Number 7 Eccles Street was a real address, empty when Joyce chose it; the house is gone now, but its door survives in the James Joyce Centre and a plaque marks the spot.
route.note: Bloom's home is 7 Eccles Street, named in the book. The Georgian house was demolished in the 1960s; the pin marks its site on the street, now beside the Mater hospital, where a plaque records it.

route.summary: Bloom rides in the funeral carriage out to the burial of Paddy Dignam, and the whole episode turns on death: graves, the gravediggers, his own dead father and son. Prospect Cemetery at Glasnevin is real and is Ireland's largest, the resting place of Parnell, O'Connell and, in time, of many Joyces.
route.note: The funeral carriage crosses the city to "Prospect," the formal name of Prospect Cemetery at Glasnevin, named elsewhere in the book. The pin marks the cemetery grounds.

route.summary: Sick of the trough-like eating houses along the way, Bloom ducks into Davy Byrne's off Grafton Street for a gorgonzola sandwich and a glass of burgundy, the quiet centre of the food-obsessed "Lestrygonians" episode. Davy Byrne's still trades at 21 Duke Street and leans hard on the association every Bloomsday.

Inside the National Library, Stephen spins his elaborate theory that Shakespeare is the ghost of Hamlet's father, sparring with the Dublin literary men while Bloom slips past outside. The library still stands on Kildare Street, its domed reading room the room Joyce knew as a student.
route.note: The episode is set in the librarian's office of the National Library on Kildare Street; the line marks Bloom passing its door. The pin is the library building itself.
